headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Gemini CLI’s filesystem/git/MCP access can collide with kotaemon’s document-processing and API-key handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts. If kotaemon content is placed in shared files or an MCP bridge, Gemini CLI may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The interaction is plausible from profiles alone, but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server
IF kotaemon ingests untrusted documents that Gemini CLI later reads as prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP for the Gemini CLI session
Require explicit human review before Gemini CLI acts on kotaemon-generated text
Use a provenance tag on all files passed between agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; kotaemon processes documents and handles API keys. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive code, transcripts, or keys can flow into a third-party inference path. The pairwise leakage pathway is credible in default-style use and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or document store
IF kotaemon sends uploaded document contents to a remote model backend
IF Gemini CLI reads files containing secrets or transcripts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Run Gemini CLI in a separate sandbox or container
Configure kotaemon to use local-only models for sensitive documents
Rotate any API keys exposed in shared workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; kotaemon also writes to ./ktem_app_data and calls multiple external APIs. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles explicitly show shared-state via filesystem/git for Gemini CLI, so conflict is likely when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or working directory
IF Gemini CLI modifies git state while kotaemon writes app data in the same tree
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Back up the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, or file edits, and kotaemon can ingest documents and citations for downstream answers. If kotaemon treats Gemini CLI output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support responses or document summaries. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show autonomous action-taking by kotaemon.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses Gemini CLI output as source material without verification
IF Gemini CLI produces incorrect facts or code that kotaemon republishes
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse
Add a human review step for imported outputs
Mark Gemini CLI outputs as untrusted in kotaemon
Compare against original source documents before publishing
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles shell environment and files in cwd, while kotaemon processes documents, transcripts, and API keys through multiple external model APIs. If regulated or sensitive documents are routed through kotaemon and then shared with Gemini CLI or remote APIs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed by kotaemon
IF those same materials are then copied into Gemini CLI or sent to remote APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools unless approved
Use local-only backends for sensitive workloads
Document retention settings for each agent
Delete temporary uploads after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
